name: Brooklyn Steel Co.
hubDetails: How SWFT Studios built a Shopify store that sells a $499 espresso machine by teaching shoppers what it does, then raises order value with bundles and accessories.
challenge: At $499, nobody buys an espresso machine on impulse. Shoppers want to know how it works and whether they can use it before they pay.
Spec sheets alone (bar pressure, grind settings) don't tell a beginner why any of it matters.
The Brooklyn café identity had to show up across the whole store, not only in the photos.
Profit depends on more than the machine, so cups and accessories needed a real place in the buying path.
built: Shopify storefront with a feature-education product page for the Talos 20 (grind settings, pressure gauge, steam wand, dual spout).
Visual feature cards that explain capabilities in benefit language, not spec sheets.
Mix-and-match bundle builder for limited-edition coffee cup collections.
Machines, Mugs, and Accessories collection pages with Brooklyn-branded typography and tone.
Brew Guides content section for post-purchase confidence.
whyMatters: If you sell something people need to understand before they buy, your website is your best salesperson. We build stores that teach, reassure and then sell.
description: How SWFT Studios built a Shopify store that sells a $499 espresso machine by teaching shoppers what it does, then raises order value with bundles and accessories.
highlight: Shopify launch: product education, bundle builder, Brew Guides
snapshot: Brooklyn Steel Co. is a kitchen appliance brand launching the Talos 20, a $499 home espresso machine with a built-in grinder and milk frother. We built their Shopify store and shaped how the product is explained, merchandised and supported after the sale.
goal: Sell a premium appliance online to people who have never used an espresso machine like it, and grow the size of each order.

approach.title: Explain the machine in plain benefits
approach.detail: We turned each feature (grind settings, pressure gauge, steam wand, dual spout) into a visual card that says what it does for your morning coffee. Shoppers who understand a product are far more likely to buy it.

approach.title: Make bundles easy to build
approach.detail: A mix and match builder for the limited edition cup collections lets shoppers add to their order in a couple of taps instead of hunting through the catalog.

approach.title: Organize the catalog the way people shop
approach.detail: Machines, Mugs and Accessories each got their own collection page with the same Brooklyn type and voice, so the store feels like one brand.

approach.title: Support the customer after checkout
approach.detail: Brew Guides give new owners recipes and how-tos. Customers who succeed with a product leave better reviews and send fewer returns.

measure: Product page conversion rate for the Talos 20 (sessions that add to cart, then purchase)
Average order value, and the share of orders that include a bundle or accessory
Traffic and time on page for Brew Guides, plus returns and support requests per order
takeaways: If your product needs explaining, your product page has to do the explaining. Lead with what it does for the buyer, then show the specs.
Bundles raise order value when they take one tap, not a second shopping trip.
Content that helps people after they buy (guides, recipes, how-tos) protects your reviews and cuts returns.

name: Manna Hydration
hubDetails: How SWFT Studios organized a fast moving drinkware catalog into a Shopify store built for seasonal drops, social traffic and repeat buyers.
challenge: New products and seasonal colors arrive often, and a growing catalog quickly starts to feel cluttered.

The brand wanted to talk about sustainability and style without slowing anyone down at checkout.
built: Shopify storefront organized by use case (Everyday Favorites, Workout Ready, Travel Essentials) and product type.
Seasonal campaign sections for launches like Summer Stripes and Color Changing Cups.
Best Sellers and New Arrivals merchandising blocks.
Instagram integration and shop-the-look experiences.
Liquid Lingo blog for hydration, wellness, and style content plus newsletter signup.
whyMatters: Lifestyle brands sell more when the store feels as alive as their Instagram feed. We build stores that make browsing fun and buying easy.
description: How SWFT Studios organized a fast moving drinkware catalog into a Shopify store built for seasonal drops, social traffic and repeat buyers.
highlight: Shopify store: seasonal drops, shop the look, blog and newsletter
snapshot: Manna Hydration sells colorful, affordable and sustainable drinkware, from color changing cups to workout bottles and everyday tumblers. We built their Shopify store around how customers actually shop: by use, by season and straight from Instagram.
goal: Turn a large, fast changing catalog and steady social traffic into repeat online sales.

approach.title: Shop by use, not only by product type
approach.detail: Collections like Everyday Favorites, Workout Ready and Travel Essentials match how people decide what to buy, so they find the right bottle faster.

approach.title: Give every drop a home
approach.detail: Campaign sections for launches like Summer Stripes and Color Changing Cups make each new release feel like an event, with Best Sellers and New Arrivals blocks to keep the homepage fresh.

approach.title: Connect Instagram to the cart
approach.detail: An Instagram feed and shop the look sections let social visitors buy what they saw in a post without searching for it.

approach.title: Bring people back
approach.detail: The Liquid Lingo blog and a newsletter signup give customers a reason to return between purchases.

measure: Revenue and conversion rate from Instagram and influencer traffic (tag links with UTM codes)
Sales in the first two weeks of each seasonal drop
Repeat purchase rate and newsletter signups per 100 visitors
takeaways: Organize products around the reason people buy them. Use cases beat long lists of SKUs.
If social media drives your traffic, every post should land on a page where the product in the post can be bought.
An email list turns one time buyers into repeat customers. Ask for the signup on every visit.

Visits from recipe pages to product pages, and support hub usage
takeaways: With a big catalog, navigation is your salesperson. Group products the way your customers think, not the way your warehouse does.
Show your products in real life. Recipes, room photos and how-tos sell better than a white background.

approach.detail: The page walks through scheduling and signup in a few clear steps, so trying it feels low effort.

approach.title: Calm, trustworthy design
approach.detail: Design tuned for reliability over hype, because people are handing over their clothes.

approach.title: One story across web and app
approach.detail: Download and signup buttons connect the website to the iOS app with the same message.

measure: App downloads and signups from the landing page
How many new users place a first order

takeaways: Describe your service through the customer's problem, not your features.
Show how easy the first step is. Most people quit at the first moment of confusion.
When people trust you with their stuff, calm and clear beats loud and clever.
